validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE — Real and under construction. P6734 is the 'Shoaiba' package of Aramco's Master Gas System Phase 3 (MGS-3) expansion. Multiple INDEPENDENT trade-press sources document this exact package: MEED ('Aramco selects contractors for Master Gas System expansion') states the Shoaiba scope is laying 56-inch, 16-inch and 10-inch lateral pipelines covering 212 km (package 14); SaudiGulfProjects' Nesma & Partners / SICIM contract-award report independently names the Shoaiba package and the 212 km / 56/16/10-inch detail; BlackRidge Research's MGS-3 project profile independently lists Shoaiba and 212 km. These are separate origins (a UK trade publication, a regional projects outlet republishing the contractor announcement, and a research-house profile), not one wire story reprinted, and none trace to GEM. Verified via url_verifier: MEED contains 'Shoaiba'+'212' (OK 200); SaudiGulfProjects contains 'Master Gas System'+'Shoaiba', '212'+'Shoaiba', and '56'+'16'+'10' (OK 200); BlackRidge contains 'Shoaiba'+'212' and '2028' (OK 200). CLASSIFICATION — Correct as gas transmission. MGS is Aramco's dry-gas trunk/lateral transmission network; the Shoaiba package is described as 56/16/10-inch lateral pipelines feeding the network. Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are both supported. DUPLICATE — Not a duplicate. P6734's 212 km / 56,10,16-in signature is unique across the 21 MGS-III rows (P6717-P6737) in the roster; no other PID shares this length+diameter, and it maps to a distinct contract package (Shoaiba, package 14). SPEC — All core specs corroborated by >=2 independent sources: length 212 km (MEED, SaudiGulfProjects, BlackRidge), diameters 56/16/10-inch (MEED, SaudiGulfProjects), status construction (program construction commenced Q2 2024 per multiple sources), start/completion 2028 (BlackRidge; aramco.com 25bn award page is the program reference but timed out under url_verifier — ReadTimeout, not a content failure), owner Aramco 100% (program is wholly Aramco). The diameter ref previously flagged as 'data value not found' on MEED was a token-matching artifact (MEED reports the three diameters separately, not the concatenated '56,10,16' string); the individual diameters are present. CAVEAT — Endpoints/exact route remain underspecified: GEM records only country-level Location (Saudi Arabia -> Saudi Arabia). Sources describe the work as concentrated in the 'Shoaiba area' (Shoaiba is on the Red Sea coast south of Jeddah, Makkah Province) but do not give discrete start/end nodes, so precise endpoints stay unverified. Hence 'confirmed (caveat)' rather than unqualified pass.
